_doc: THE SOL COLOURS — the seven colours read from Sol LeWitt's late acrylic wall drawings, NAMED (decibel PLAN 2.2; RUNNING_LOG §307; DEC-90: 'ok lets just assign them resonable names SOL_'). The prefix as his own colours carry `clr`. The names are the AI's, plain hue names; the values the AI's pick from the reading (bank/palette/lewitt_reading.json) — `from` says which number and why. His to rename or move: edit a row, then `node tools/palette/build_page.js`. A colour DERIVED FROM photographs, never a measurement of the paint (§304).

colours.name: SOL_red
colours.from: all photographs, evened (9) — the white-wall photographs alone give #CF1824, two units away
colours.chart: nearest on the maker's chart: 125 Cadmium red light · 127 Cadmium red medium · 126 Pyrrole red — not separable

colours.name: SOL_orange
colours.from: the AI's reading of the clean evidence (§305): hue 42–43° in Loopy Doopy and in the square-on photograph of 1112. The two computed means (#DF3123 · #DC3821) carry one warm photograph and sit so near SOL_red that the pair would not read as two colours in a score
colours.chart: a red-orange: 125 Cadmium red light · 124 Cadmium orange deep · 123 Pyrrole orange — not the chart's oranges

colours.name: SOL_yellow
colours.from: the white-wall photographs (5) — they agree within 2.5

colours.name: SOL_green
colours.from: all photographs, evened (7) — the white-wall photographs alone give a lighter, yellower #38AA54
colours.chart: nearest: 154 Phthalo green light · 161 Cobalt nickel green · 156 Cadmium green medium

colours.name: SOL_blue
colours.from: all photographs, evened (9) — the white-wall photographs alone give a lighter #2479CC; two photographs of ONE wall differ by twelve units of lightness
colours.chart: no shade of the chart is near

colours.name: SOL_purple
colours.from: all photographs, evened (9) — the white-wall photographs alone give #67469C
colours.chart: bluer and lighter than either Dioxazine violet as printed
